rich_summary: This section links the power of Brahmanical spiritual authority with divine warfare and culminates in Bhishma’s theological praise of Krishna. The narrative begins with Vedic mantras destroying the Kapas; although the gods defeat the Danavas in battle, Narada reveals that the real victory was achieved through the energy of Brahmanas. Arjuna affirms his lifelong devotion to Brahmanas and attributes his own power to the grace of Dattatreya, while the wind-god instructs him to protect them as a sacred Kshatriya duty and warns of a future danger from the Bhrigu race. In the following dialogue, Bhishma—aware that death is near—directs Yudhishthira to Krishna for ultimate answers and delivers a sweeping declaration of Krishna’s cosmic identity as creator, sustainer, and restorer of righteousness. The passage emphasizes the hierarchy of spiritual power and Krishna’s supreme, all-encompassing divinity.

highlight_spans.why: The opening image of Vedic mantras shining like golden clouds after destroying the Kapas establishes the theme that spiritual power, not merely martial strength, wins cosmic battles.
Arjuna’s declaration that he lives for and worships the Brahmanas reveals the ideological foundation of the section: the Kshatriya’s duty to uphold and protect spiritual authority.
The wind-god’s instruction to protect Brahmanas as one protects one’s own senses states the ethical command binding warrior power to priestly sanctity.
Bhishma’s admission that the time to cast off his body approaches gives the discourse emotional gravity and frames his speech as a final testament.
The statement that all creation has flowed from Krishna encapsulates Bhishma’s sweeping theological claim of Krishna’s cosmic supremacy.

top_scenes.scene_text: Vedic mantras blaze across the sky like luminous golden clouds as unseen spiritual power destroys the Kapas while the gods battle below.
Bhishma lying on his bed of arrows, pale and near death, raising his head to proclaim Krishna as the cosmic source of creation before Yudhishthira and the gathered warriors.
Narada descending among the assembled gods, revealing that the Brahmanas’ spiritual energy—not the gods’ weapons—truly destroyed their enemies.
